feedback.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we have 

$$
{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{f(x)-{x}^{2}}{{f}^{′}(x)+2{e}^{x}}=\frac{{lim}_{x\to 0}\,(f(x)-{x}^{2})}{{lim}_{x\to 0}\,({f}^{′}(x)+2{e}^{x})}.
$$

We find from the graph that ${lim}_{x\to 0}\,f(x)=f(0)=0$ and ${lim}_{x\to 0}\,{f}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(0)=-1.$ Calculating the limits of the numerator and denominator separately, we have

$$
\begin{aligned} & {lim}_{x\to 0}\,(f(x)-{x}^{2})=0+{0}^{2}=0, \\  & {lim}_{x\to 0}\,({f}^{′}(x)+2{e}^{x})=-1+2=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Taking the quotient of these limits, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\,\frac{f(x)-{x}^{2}}{{f}^{′}(x)+2{e}^{x}} & =\frac{{lim}_{x\to 0}\,(f(x)-{x}^{2})}{{lim}_{x\to 0}\,({f}^{′}(x)+2{e}^{x})} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
